newsitem.title: UK: Bond market wrapup - late European trade.
newsitem.headline: Bond market wrapup - late European trade.

text.p: This is how major world bond markets looked at 1630 GMT on Tuesday.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries traded near unchanged after an early drop. Retail sales for June looked strong at first, sparking selling across the yield curve. Sales rose 0.5 percent, exceeding the forecast for a 0.2-percent increase.
May retail sales were revised down to a 0.3 percent decline from a 0.1 percent drop originally.
U.S. Treasury prices had opened lower as participants took profits and adjusted positions ahead of the sales report.
Futures: September T-bonds at 113-23/32, down 7/32
September Eurodollars at 94.22, unchanged
Cash: Long bond yield 6.56 percent.
GERMANY - German Bunds, futures ended lower and under pressure on spreads. September futures were also hurt by technical factors, after a break of support at 102.30. Next support 102.15.
Futures: September Bunds on LIFFE at 102.29, down 0.38
September Euromarks at 96.76, down 0.02
Cash: 10-year Bund yield 5.62 percent.

BRITAIN - UK gilts ended 2/32 lower on Tuesday after dipping in line with falling European bond markets, but the losses were stemmed by the Bank of England's announcement that next week's 8.0 percent gilt auction will be a smaller-than-expected 2.0 billion sterling.
"Gilts have been quite resilient in the face of downward pressure in Europe," said a gilts salesman. "They were helped by the fact the auction will only be 2.0 billion stg."
Futures: September Long gilts on LIFFE at 114.06, down 0.12
September Eurosterling at 92.84, unchanged
Cash: 10-year gilt yield 7.09 percent.
FRANCE - French bonds suffered along with the German market on Tuesday, closing lower as concern about European monetary union drove up the dollar.
French traders were also catching up after the long holiday weekend and the market remained relatively calm as strong liquidity stemmed fears of a bigger sell-off.
Futures: September Long bond on MATIF at 130.04, up 0.06
September PIBOR at 96.49, unchanged
Cash: 10-year bond (OAT) yield 5.48 percent.

ITALY - Italy's debt market ended sharply lower, weighed down by a super-strong dollar and profit-taking, the second consecutive session which saw Btp futures slide more than other European bond markets.
Traders said the main factor was the strength of the dollar, steady above 1.80 marks, which was blurring the future scenario of the single European currency.
Futures: September Long bond on LIFFE at 135.53, down 0.76
September Eurolira at 93.32, down 0.01
Cash: 10-year bond (BTP) yield 6.54 percent.
JAPAN - The key September futures JGB contract ended lower on Tuesday due to strong 4.5 percent month-on-month growth in revised May industrial output, traders said.
The JGBs also fell on a foreign media report that newly appointed MOF Vice Minister Eisuke Sakakibara said market views on the economy are still too pessimistic.
Futures: September JGB future on LIFFE compared with Tokyo close at 124.58, down 0.38.
September Euroyen at 99.32.
Cash: 10-year JGB yield 2.54 percent.
EUROBONDS - Continuing the pattern seen in recent weeks, the Eurobond market saw further jumbo dollar bonds launched on Tuesday.

Triple-A rated car manufacturer Toyota Motor Corp issued a $1.0 billion five-year bond in Asia, which will be priced later to yield 10 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes. CSFB and Merrill Lynch were joint lead managers.
